ORIGIN.quote: The logs do not distinguish one operator launching many workers from multiple researchers running the same agent environment, and “Anthropic”/“Claude” strings are self-assertions, not provenance. Attribution to any model vendor is **Low confidence** and should not be made from this evidence.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader learns that the corpus contains Anthropic/Claude self-identifications and that the report deliberately refuses to treat them as evidence of provenance, so the takeaway is that vendor attribution has been set aside rather than that Anthropic is a live candidate operator. This sits at 0.4 rather than 0.6 because Anthropic is never left standing as an open possibility, and above 0.2 because the report does explicitly connect the Anthropic strings to the question of where the swarm came from before dismissing them.
